_meta.status: Draft — expanded from 2-room stub. Requires sign-off from a licensed Vastu consultant before production use.
_meta.epistemic_note: Vastu Shastra is a traditional Indian belief system, not an empirically validated science. Rules below reflect consensus positions across multiple independent Indian Vastu-consultancy sources (cross-referenced, not single-sourced). Where sources genuinely disagreed, the conflict is recorded in 'notes' rather than silently resolved. Remedies are traditional/folk practices, not medically or scientifically proven interventions.
_meta.zone_calculation: 16 zones = 8 cardinal/ordinal directions each split into 2 sub-zones of 22.5° (360/16). Accurate zoning requires a true compass reading anchored to the plot's geometric center (Brahmasthan), not the building's visual center.

severity_levels.major: Widely flagged across sources as a serious dosha (defect) — significant risk of being cited in a professional audit as a compliance failure. Structural correction is the only complete fix; remedies mitigate, they don't cure.
severity_levels.minor: Suboptimal but tolerated in most traditions, or disputed across sources. Remedies are generally considered effective.

remedy.S: South-facing entrances are traditionally corrected via an offset/zigzag entry path, a Vastu pyramid or Ganesha idol at the threshold, and bright, constant lighting — not a full fix, mitigation only.

MainEntrance.notes: Strong cross-source consensus on N/NE/E as most auspicious. South entrance is the most consistently discouraged; door should open inward, clockwise.

remedy.NE: Traditional remedy: yellow or light-colored (e.g. Jaisalmer yellow marble) flooring under the stove, cook facing east, and keep the NE corner of the kitchen visually light and uncluttered.
remedy.SW: Traditional remedy: place the stove/cooking platform on the SE wall of the kitchen even if the room itself is in SW, and use earth-tone (terracotta, ochre) tiling.

Kitchen.notes: SE (Agni Kona) is the near-universal first choice across sources. NW is the most commonly cited secondary option. Sources disagree on whether N is 'forbidden' or merely 'not ideal' — treated here as minor.

MasterBedroom.sleeping_direction: Head towards South or East; sleeping with head towards North is the one point sources most consistently advise against.

remedy.NE: Traditional remedy: earth-tone/heavy textiles, grounding colors, avoid placing the bed directly in the NE corner even within an NE-zoned room.
remedy.SE: SE carries fire energy per tradition; remedy is to avoid red/orange bedroom palettes and keep electrical equipment away from the bed.

MasterBedroom.notes: SW consensus is very strong (stability, Earth element, head of household). SE is discouraged for bedrooms generally, not just master.

remedy.SE: Cooling colors (blue, green, white) to counter the fire-zone energy attributed to SE.

ChildrenBedroom.notes: Lower source-consensus than master bedroom/kitchen; treat this room's rules as lower-confidence.

GuestBedroom.notes: NW is associated with transient/movement energy — considered ideal for guests who are meant to stay temporarily, not indefinitely.

LivingRoom.layout_rule: Heavy furniture (sofas, cabinets) along S/W walls; keep N/E sides relatively open for light and circulation.
LivingRoom.notes: No 'forbidden' zone found with strong consensus for living rooms — this is a flexible room across sources.

DiningRoom.seating_rule: Family should ideally face East while eating.
DiningRoom.notes: Weaker/lower-volume source agreement than kitchen or bedroom placements — flagged as medium confidence, needs consultant sign-off before being treated as a hard rule.

remedy.shares_wall_with_toilet: Sources are unanimous this is one of the worst compound defects and consistently recommend relocation over any cosmetic remedy; cosmetic mitigations (mirror facing the pooja room, sealing the shared wall) are described as partial only.

PoojaRoom.notes: This is a compound-constraint room: the forbidden list includes structural adjacencies, not just compass zones. Represented here as special string flags rather than pure zone codes — the audit engine needs a separate adjacency-check pass for this.

remedy.NE: Most-cited remedies: sea salt bowl replaced weekly, keep door closed at all times, indoor plant (money plant/spider plant), extreme cleanliness. Sources are explicit that no remedy fully removes this dosha — relocation during renovation is the only complete fix, and the product should not claim otherwise.
remedy.SW: Vastu pyramid on the outer SW wall; light yellow/beige interior color; keep door closed.

Toilet.wall_sharing_rule: Should not share a wall with the kitchen, bedroom (behind the bed), or pooja room.
Toilet.seat_direction: Person should face North or South while seated; never East or West.
Toilet.notes: Genuine cross-source conflict on the single 'best' zone: some sources say N/NW, others say W-of-NW or S/SW-adjacent (e.g. AppliedVastu). NE and SW are the only two zones where 'forbidden + major severity' is essentially unanimous. 'center' (Brahmasthan) is separately and universally forbidden for any toilet.
Toilet.confidence: high (for forbidden zones) / medium (for single best preferred zone)

remedy.NE: Reduce visual/structural weight in the NE — sources generally treat this as requiring redesign rather than a cosmetic fix.

Staircase.notes: Consensus: stairs should be heavy/grounded, so S/SW/W (Earth-associated zones) are preferred; NE (light, sacred zone) and the exact plot center are both avoided.

remedy.SW: Desk oriented so the person faces East or North regardless of room zone.

StudyRoom.notes: Desk-facing direction is cited more consistently than the room's own zone placement.

StoreRoom.notes: Heavy storage generally pushed to SW-adjacent sub-zones; kept light in NE.

remedy.NE: Paint tank blue; relocate to SW where structurally feasible.

OverheadWaterTank.notes: Distinguish from underground sump/borewell, which follows the opposite rule (see WaterSumpBorewell).

WaterSumpBorewell.notes: Underground water storage follows the opposite placement logic from overhead tanks — do not conflate the two in the audit engine.

remedy.default: Paint blue; relocate away from NE/S where feasible.

SepticTank.notes: Lower source volume specifically on septic tanks vs. general toilet rules; confidence downgraded accordingly.

Garage.notes: Garage/vehicle-parking rules had the least source depth of all rooms searched — treat as provisional pending consultant review.

shape.notes: Consistent across sources: square/rectangular plots are auspicious; irregular shapes require either structural correction or are advised against outright.

floor_slope.rule: Ground level should be higher in SW, sloping down towards NE.

brahmasthan.rule: The geometric center of the plot should be kept open, light, and free of heavy structure (no toilet, staircase, or heavy pillar in the exact center).

known_gaps: No numeric compass-degree ingestion logic defined yet — zones here are categorical (16 labels), but the audit engine needs the actual 0-360° reading plus plot-center coordinates to assign a room to a zone correctly.
No handling for multi-story buildings (zone rules can shift by floor in some traditions — not covered here).

Ayadi/Vastu Purusha Mandala numerological calculations (plot proportions, entrance-point auspiciousness by measurement) are a distinct, more advanced layer not included in this schema — flag to product/legal whether the product's marketing claims 'full Vastu compliance' (which would require this) or 'directional Vastu audit' (which this schema supports).

Legal/compliance: remedy language throughout should be reviewed by legal before shipping, since 'this will fix your dosha' claims (as opposed to 'this is a traditional remedy for X') carry consumer-protection risk in a paid product.
